extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers and critics of literature and Christian Science (late-19th-century literary criticism audience)
extracted.subtask_short: literary critique of Christian Science writings
extracted.subtask_description: A satirical/critical essay examining the authorship, style, and literary quality of Mary Baker G. Eddy's writings (Science and Health and related texts), and discussing standards for prayer and religious writing. Focuses on textual evidence, clarity, and moral effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality of English prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Has never been able to write anything above third-rate English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a broad measure of authorial competence; contrasted with 'easy and flowing and direct English' in other exhibits. Anti-patterns: labored, lumbering, confused gropings; sentences that do not read as natural English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak in the matter of grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor grammar is cited as direct evidence of limited literary ability. Evaluate for basic grammatical correctness and conventional usage; anti-patterns include frequent grammatical errors that impede comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of the value of words (diction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has but a rude and dull sense of the values of words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess word-choice sensitivity and precision. Good prose uses words with appropriate connotation and nuance; bad prose uses words clumsily or inaptly, dulling meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary precision and clarity of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: So lacks in the matter of literary precision that she can seldom put a thought into words that express it lucidly to the reader and leave no doubts in his mind as to whether he has rightly understood or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: can the writer render ideas so clearly that readers reliably understand intended meaning? Anti-patterns: ambiguous phrasing, confused constructions, sentences whose meaning cannot be restated with confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensibility of prefaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Cannot even draught a Preface that a person can fully comprehend, nor one which can by any art be translated into a fully understandable form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefaces should orient the reader clearly; evaluate whether a preface communicates purpose and contents straightforwardly. Anti-patterns: opaque prefaces, sentences that resist paraphrase or translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level paraphrasability / unambiguous meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: A reader should be able to take a sentence apart, examine it word by word, and find sentences whose meanings he is so sure of that he can rephrase them in his own words and reproduce those meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paraphraseability as a test of clarity. Guidance: if a large fraction of sentences resist faithful paraphrase, this indicates poor writing. Example anti-pattern: losing money trying to play the paraphrase game on unclear sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and analytical quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Known and undisputed writings exhibit no depth, no analytical quality, no thought above school composition size, and but juvenile ability in handling thoughts of even that modest magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the sophistication of ideas, presence of analysis, and intellectual maturity. Anti-patterns: writing that reads like school composition, lacks argument structure, or displays juvenile handling of topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to write functional/commercial/technical prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Although she has fine commercial ability and could draught rules, their English would discredit a lowly clerk; she cannot write well upon any subject, even a commercial one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, precision, and practicality in technical or rule-based writing. Anti-patterns: rules or by-laws written in poor English that would embarrass a clerk; lack of functional clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic consistency / single-author provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare labored and lumbering Preface with easy, flowing, direct English elsewhere to judge whether the same hand and brain produced both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stylistic comparison across sections (preface vs. chapter, different editions) to assess claims of single authorship. Evidence of marked stylistic heterogeneity supports alternative authorship hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of textual evidence to test authorship claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The treacherous testimony of her own pen in known and undisputed productions can be used to judge whether she originated the thoughts and reasonings of the larger book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply forensic literary observation: compare known samples to contested text for grammar, diction, syntax, and expressive capacity. Anti-patterns: accepting authorship claims without comparing stylistic fingerprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative quality across editions/sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should compare different passages and editions (e.g., Preface vs. Prayer chapter) to decide whether quality and style are consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate changes between editions and sections; a markedly superior passage among inferior ones suggests different authorship or revision. Example: Appendix exhibits contrasted pieces for reader comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and sufficiency in autobiographical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: An autobiographical paragraph that excuses meagerness and poor quality by claiming restraint (Divine etiquette) is suspect; an autobiography should provide sufficient, candid detail for its subject and fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an autobiographical work supplies adequate factual and personal detail appropriate to its subject; anti-pattern: deliberate withholding excused by high-minded claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between claimed mode of composition and textual quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that works were extemporaneously written or dictated, and that an amanuensis was employed, should be weighed against the text's quality and polish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author claims extemporaneity but produces polished, internally consistent, and mature prose, reconcile the claim; conversely, poor prose is more consistent with extemporaneous composition. Use such claims as auxiliary evidence in authorship/style judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of prayer measured by moral/behavioral change
rubrics_metrics.description: The test of all prayer lies in whether we love our neighbor better and change our behavior because of the asking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prayers by outcomes: do they produce sincere reform, increased love, and consistent moral action? Anti-patterns: prayers that result only in feeling or verbal piety without changed conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity over formality in prayer (avoid verbalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audible or long verbal prayers, ecclesiasticism, and creeds often materialize worship and may impede spiritual growth; silent prayer, watchfulness, and devout obedience enable true following of Jesus' example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize internal disposition and sustained practice over ornate or verbose outward prayers. Anti-patterns: long, performative prayers that substitute for inward reformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repentance requires reformation, not mere sorrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Sorrow for wrong-doing is only the first step; the true test of sincerity is reformation—actual change under the stress of circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure repentance by observable change and resistance to temptation; anti-pattern: believing sorrow or confession alone suffices for moral repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct motives and faith for petitionary prayer
rubrics_metrics.description: We 'ask amiss' when petitions seek to consume on lusts; petitions only bring results proportionate to the petitioner's faith and right motive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the moral orientation of requests; self-serving petitions are likely ineffective. Use scriptural caution: some requests are denied because they would be harmful or misdirected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hypocrisy and wordy prayers
rubrics_metrics.description: A wordy prayer may give a sense of self-justification while masking hypocrisy; audible professions can 'cover a multitude of sins'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prayers for congruence between profession and conduct. Anti-patterns: verbose prayer used as moral cover; external piety inconsistent with private behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid emotionalism as a substitute for spiritual sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical sensation and ecstatic emotions are not equivalent to spiritual understanding; if ecstatic moments are not guided by spiritual sense, they produce transient effects only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between outward emotional displays and inward spiritual growth. Anti-pattern: equating strong feeling with durable spiritual attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure religious writing by long-term efficacy, not momentary impressiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Audible prayer or impressive religious language may elevate thought momentarily but must be judged by lasting benefit and actual spiritual progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize whether a text/practice leads to sustained moral/spiritual improvement over whether it produces immediate solemnity or excitement.
